title: Eventual smoothness of a finitely presented algebraic space
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; quasi-compactness means that affine scheme tests have quasi-compact inverse images, and quasi-separatedness means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Separatedness means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set [def-weil-size-convention], $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps and limit $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented algebraic space $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$. Put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$ for $i\geq i_0$ and $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. If $X\to T$ is smooth, there is $j\geq i_0$ such that $X_i\to T_i$ is smooth for every $i\geq j$. No surjectivity of transition maps or Noetherianity assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CN2 (lemma-descend-smooth), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space over affine scheme bases. Persistence: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZE (lemma-base-change-smooth).

proof.text: The affine test $T_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ in quasi-compactness of $f_{i_0}$ shows that $X_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a_0:U_0\to X_{i_0}$ with $U_0$ affine. Apply the presentation criterion to $f_{i_0}$, with target chart the identity of $T_{i_0}$ and property local finite presentation. This is an etale-local scheme property by the cited scheme-locality theorem. Thus $h_0=f_{i_0}a_0:U_0\to T_{i_0}$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0CN2 (lemma-descend-smooth), choice of affine presentations; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover)

proof.text: For $i\geq i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, and put $U=U_0\times_{T_{i_0}}T$. The universal property of the sheaf fibre product identifies these with $U_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$ and $U_0\times_{X_{i_0}}X$. Base change of an etale cover therefore gives representable surjective etale maps $a_i:U_i\to X_i$ and $a:U\to X$. These sources are schemes because they are base changes of the representable atlas. Apply the presentation criterion for smoothness to $X\to T$, with target chart the identity of $T$; the scheme-locality theorem verifies its hypothesis on smoothness. It follows that the composite $h:U\to T$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0CN2 (lemma-descend-smooth), base-changed diagrams and smoothness on presentations; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target)

proof.text: Restrict the base diagram to the nonempty directed tail $J=\{i\in I:i\geq i_0\}$. Its limit is still $T$: a cone on the tail extends to $T_k$ by choosing $l\geq k,i_0$ and composing its $l$-component with $T_l\to T_k$; two choices agree by passing to a common upper bound. This also proves uniqueness and the limiting universal property. Apply affine-diagram smoothness descent with $D_i=T_i$ for $i\in J$, $Q=T_{i_0}$, $P=U_0$, structural maps $T_i\to T_{i_0}$ and $T\to T_{i_0}$, and $p=h_0$. Both $P,Q$ and every $D_i$ are affine; $h_0$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1, and its limit pullback is the smooth map $h$ of step 2. Hence there is $j\geq i_0$ for which $h_j:U_j\to T_j$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0CN2 (lemma-descend-smooth), final reduction to limits.tex Tag 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), affine case

proof.text: Fix any $i\geq j$. The universal property of fibre products gives $U_i\simeq U_j\times_{T_j}T_i$, compatibly with projections to $T_i$: both sides represent pairs consisting of a point of $U_0$ and a point of $T_i$ with the same image in $T_{i_0}$. Thus $h_i$ is the base change of $h_j$, and is smooth by scheme smooth base change. The diagram with source chart $a_i:U_i\to X_i$ and target chart $\operatorname{id}_{T_i}$ is a presentation with surjective source chart by step 2. The presentation criterion for smoothness, whose etale-locality hypothesis is verified by the scheme-locality theorem, now gives smoothness of $X_i\to T_i$. This holds for every $i\geq j$.

lean.statement: theorem eventually_smooth_of_affine_isLimit {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over S) (hD : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffine (D.obj i).left) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit ((Over.forget S).mapCone c)) (i₀ : I) (X₀ : AlgebraicSpace S) (f₀ : X₀.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (D.obj (op i₀))) (hlfp : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@LocallyOfFinitePresentation) X₀ (D.obj (op i₀)) f₀) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f₀) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f₀)) (hf : HasEtalePresentationProperty (@Smooth) (Limits.pullback.snd f₀ (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i₀))))) : ∃ (j : I) (hj : i₀ ≤ j), ∀ (i : I) (hi : j ≤ i), HasEtalePresentationProperty (@Smooth) (Limits.pullback.snd f₀ (yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE (hj.trans hi)).op)))
lean.note: The base diagram is in Over S, with its cone limiting on underlying schemes. MapToSchemeIsLocally and MapIsQuasiCompact give the existing local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and diagonal quasi-compactness notions. HasEtalePresentationProperty Smooth expresses smoothness of the canonical presheaf pullback projections, equivalently the sheaf fibre product projections. All bases are affine, so affine transition maps are automatic.
